newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN FAFER MARKED HIGHER ON SALE TALK.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN FAFER MARKED HIGHER ON SALE TALK.

text.p: Shares in Belgian stainless steel company Fabrique de Fer (Fafer) were marked sharply higher on the Brussels bourse on Friday following a newspaper report the company was about to be sold.

In pre-bourse trade, the share's bid/ask was indicated at 200,000 Belgian francs, up from 109,000 francs at Thursday's close. Fafer is listed on Brussels cash market where prices are fixed twice a day around 1100 (0900 GMT) and 1500 (1300 GMT).

Belgian newspaper Le Soir said on Friday that Fafer's main shareholder, Belgium's Boel family, was considering selling its stake in the company because Fafer's current size meant its long-term future could not be guaranteed.
Le Soir said possible buyers included British Steel , Belgian-Luxembourg group Arbed/Sidmar and France's Usinor-Sacilor .
Analysts recently said shares in Fafer and its shareholder Belgian holding company Henex -- part of the Boel family- controlled Boel Group -- were undervalued and should be bought.
